clue.text: Nonsense heard repeatedly in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a British word for empty talk or rubbish
the word stage extras mutter over and over to sound like a murmuring crowd

explanation.surface: Someone complains of the drivel heard night after night on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drivel, and it is also the word actors in a crowd scene chant to simulate background chatter.

clue.text: On the other side shed excess population

parts.note: over means across, on the far side
to spill is to shed or let fall

explanation.surface: Across the border, a country sheds its surplus people.
explanation.walkthrough: In British planning, this is the population that moves out of a crowded city into new towns nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Planners use the word for people rehoused outside an overcrowded town.

clue.text: It is gritty during wet weather in outskirts of Grimsby

indicators.note: in says the wet-weather word sits inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of Grimsby

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Someone says Grimsby feels gritty when it rains on the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Grimsby is a fishing port on England's east coast; only its first and last letters, G and Y, are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of grains or particles has a gritty texture.

clue.text: Purchase, but no payment is necessary

definitions.text: Purchase, but no payment is necessary

parts.words: Purchase, but no payment is necessary
parts.note: purchase here means a mechanical grip or advantage, not buying something, so no money changes hands

explanation.surface: A shopper is delighted to get something for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in its physical sense is the grip or advantage gained by a lever-like tool.

clue.text: The coolness of one trained in deportment?

definitions.text: The coolness of one trained in deportment?

parts.words: The coolness of one trained in deportment?
parts.note: deportment pupils famously walked balancing books on their heads, keeping the head perfectly flat, which also suggests calm composure

explanation.surface: A finishing-school pupil shows admirable composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and calm good sense, pictured literally as a head held flat.

clue.text: Sue could be, between five and six, with us on the mountain

indicators.note: between places the rearranged letters inside the two numerals

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: could be says the letters of Sue may take another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sue may be up on the mountain with us between five and six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SUE to ESU, and 'between' puts ESU inside V and VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous volcano near Naples is a mountain.

clue.text: Lover of Shakespeare

parts.note: reads like a fan of the playwright, but means a lover created by him, the hero of a tragedy set in Verona

explanation.surface: A fan of the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Montague who loves Juliet is Shakespeare's best-known romantic hero.

clue.text: Is this craft used for shooting the rapids?

definitions.text: Is this craft used for shooting the rapids?

parts.words: Is this craft used for shooting the rapids?
parts.note: shooting the rapids means riding white water, but here shooting means firing guns from a vessel

explanation.surface: An adventurer asks which boat suits white-water rafting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small armed vessel is a craft built for shooting.

clue.text: Young person's hair-remover

definitions.meaning: a young ... is old slang for a lad

explanation.surface: A youngster's razor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a youngster and also names an electric razor.

clue.text: Undergarment intended, so to speak, to be a ceremonial garment

parts.note: a vest is a British undershirt

indicators.note: so to speak signals that a word is said out loud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: An undershirt was supposedly meant as formal robes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is worn under a shirt; 'so to speak' turns MEANT into its sound-alike MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe worn by clergy at services is a ceremonial garment.

clue.text: Unsuccessful conjuring with a bit over

indicators.note: conjuring is magic trickery, so the letters of a bit over are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A magician's trick failed because it ran a little long.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt that comes to nothing is a failed, fruitless one.

clue.text: Against dove in Scotland consuming eggs in witchcraft!.

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
doo is the Scots word for a dove or pigeon
O looks like an egg, so two eggs give OO

explanation.surface: A Scottish dove eats eggs as part of a magic ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts OO between V and DOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean folk religion is associated with spells and sorcery.

clue.text: Fall over Oriental heard taking church set of three panels

parts.note: to trip is to stumble or fall over

indicators.note: heard says the word for the Asian person is spelt by its sound

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand in Asia

explanation.surface: Someone trips over an Asian visitor while carrying church panels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns THAI into the sound-alike TY.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece made of three hinged painted boards is a three-panel work.

clue.text: Identity of a beginner in the union

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the union's name

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A newcomer's identity card for the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and L inside EQUITY. Equity is the trade union for British actors, and L comes from the plates learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity in its sense of exact sameness means being equal in every respect.

clue.text: Sweet drink on the rocks?

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
rocks is bar slang for ice cubes

explanation.surface: A sweet drink served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'on the rocks' is the barman's phrase; here 'on' just puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The black chewy confection is a type of sweet, British for a candy.

clue.text: Risings between France and Spain

parts.note: risings suggests uprisings or revolts, but means rising ground, the high peaks on the border

explanation.surface: Rebellions break out on the Franco-Spanish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range forms the natural frontier between the two countries.

clue.text: Used to be working

definitions.meaning: made use of, as a tool is put to use

explanation.surface: Someone recalls they once had a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both made use of and having paid work.

clue.text: Moderate youth leader displays humility

parts.note: modest means moderate, not excessive

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A temperate young team captain shows humility.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person shows humility and lack of vanity.

clue.text: Detailed analysis of a cat in any environment

indicators.note: in shows the cat sits inside the other word
environment means surroundings, so any surrounds the cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A study examines a cat in all kinds of settings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean a close dissection or examination of any subject.

clue.text: Industrial waste flowing out

definitions.meaning: liquid discharge from factories or sewage works
an adjective for something that flows forth

explanation.surface: Factory waste is pouring away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both factory discharge and an adjective for streaming forth.

clue.text: Firework to give a hissing sound on the carriage

parts.note: to fiz is to fizz or hiss
a gig is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A firework hisses on top of a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old name for a hissing kind of firework or squib.

clue.text: Wholesome bid Lee moved

indicators.note: moved signals that the letters of bid Lee are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Lee made a healthy offer at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Food fit to eat is wholesome enough to consume.

clue.text: Stick with the umpire's decision?

definitions.meaning: a short rod, as carried by a conductor or relay runner
in cricket, an umpire ruling a batsman not out lets them carry on batting

explanation.surface: A player abides by the referee's call.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman given not out by the umpire continues to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rod is a stick, and read as two words it describes carrying on at the crease.

clue.text: Two extreme characters involved with hen and rat running wild in Israel

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so all the letters are scrambled

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A hen and a rat run riot over two odd figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' rearranges A, Z, HEN and RAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: The town where Jesus grew up lies in northern Israel; the definition names where it is.

clue.text: Others, ie removed the line on the map

indicators.note: removed means moved about, so the letters of others and ie are reordered

explanation.surface: Other people, that is, rubbed out the map's line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a contour on a weather map joining places with the same mean summer temperature.

clue.text: Entrance money

definitions.meaning: an old sense of a coming in or arrival

explanation.surface: An admission fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are money coming in, and the word once meant an arrival or entry.

clue.text: His pony's affected by semi-consciousness

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's pony is in a dazed state.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of the possessive counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance-like state between sleep and waking.
